title: Values of the payment-matching access profile that the legacy story does not state
source: WP B2-P4-021; legacy RWB-E2-027 sections 3, 10, 12; FSD P4 v3 A2.4, A2.6, A2.7; TSD P4 v3 T3.2, T6.1
description: The legacy story fixes the letters of the four roles for two capability areas and leaves everything else open: the matrix version label in force, the letters of any other area for the same roles, the letters of the agent identity SY-AGENT in WRITE_OFF_AND_POSTING, the parameter set of the profile, and the database login name. The story is written with the values that the FSD and TSD of module P4 do state (matrix versions PM-2026.11 and PM-2026.12, LOV-CAPABILITY areas WRITE_OFF_AND_POSTING and RULES_AND_PARAMETERS) and with the placeholder phrase for the rest.
evidence: Legacy section 10 names RW-CREDITAD Write-off and posting CRUA, RW-FINANCE Write-off and posting RA, RW-COE Rules and parameters C and RW-RISK Rules and parameters A, and nothing else; legacy sections 3 and 12 name no matrix version. FSD P4 AC-P4-004-01 names matrix versions PM-2026.11 and PM-2026.12; TSD P4 T3.2 names the 14 capability areas.
proposed: Take the matrix versions and the area codes from the FSD and TSD of P4; keep the four legacy letters unchanged; record the SY-AGENT letters and the login name as open and confirm them with the security administrator before the wave 2 test set is signed.

title: DP-added platform and published contracts are not in the metadata dependency rows
source: WP B2-P4-021; Template and Rules v1 R5.5, R5.7 and R7.1
description: The DP table adds H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON, H RWB-PLT-E1047-CON, H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON, H RWB-PLT-N001-CON and C RWB-P3-E1043-CON, and the DP-04 and DP-06 rows would add H RWB-PLT-E1072-CON, H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON, C RWB-P7-E1073-CON and C RWB-P3-E1042-CON if the story used them. The metadata rows of the story are fixed by the WP as Depends on (build) None and Contract dependencies RWB-P8-E2027-CON only. The story is written to the fixed rows, builds against the published platform set and the fakes, and states in section 13 which rows it does not use.
evidence: WP B2-P4-021 story line: H [], C [RWB-P8-E2027-CON]. Template and Rules v1 R5.5 rows DP-03, DP-06, DP-07, DP-10, DP-14, DP-15, DP-19 and R5.7 rule 3 (H points to the same service or a platform CON).
proposed: Keep the metadata rows as the WP fixes them; carry the platform and rwb-case contracts as build-against dependencies of section 13 and confirm at the wave 2 planning gate that no H chain is missing from the lane.

title: The rule-package endpoints are P4 in the legacy contract and P7 in Arch v5
source: WP B2-P4-021; legacy RWB-E2-027 section 12; TSD P4 v3 T-A.1 API-P4-014 to API-P4-019; context pack P4 ownership rows; Arch v5 slides 4, 5 and 13
description: The legacy story calls POST and GET /api/recovery/v1/admin/rule-packages/PAYMENT_MATCH/versions as P4 operations, and TSD P4 T-A.1 still lists the six rule-package and rule-version endpoints as P4. Arch v5 and the ownership map give the rule registry to P7 rwb-decision, and the P4 ownership rows are the four admin and session operations only. Under R-PREC the Arch v5 rows win: the endpoints are P7's and P4 supplies the right that gates them. The story keeps the legacy judgement (who may load, who may approve) and drops the endpoint ownership.
evidence: Context pack P4 REST operations provided: GET /admin/access-log, GET /admin/roles, GET /me/session, POST /admin/break-glass-grants. Legacy section 12 publishes the same two rule-package paths as P4. Arch v5 slide 4 places the decision centre and log with P7 and slide 13 gives P4 a REST call to ACE Common only.
proposed: Publish the rule-package and rule-version operations from RWB-P7-E2027-APP and RWB-P7-E2042-APP only; P4 keeps the loader and approver rights of section 10 and the refusals of AC3 and AC6; correct TSD P4 T-A.1 at the next version.

title: No legacy acceptance criterion of RWB-E2-027 belongs to the P4 slice
source: WP B2-P4-021; legacy RWB-E2-027 section 7; Template and Rules v1 R7.2 s7 and the WP item 4
description: The WP gives the story an empty acs list, so no legacy criterion is copied: AC1 to AC10 of the legacy story test the match itself and are owned by RWB-P8-E2027-APP, and the two access test cases TC-E2-027-11 and TC-E2-027-12 have no criterion of their own in the legacy set. The seven criteria of this story are therefore new under D-RCV-60 and test only the access profile; the thirteen legacy test cases keep their IDs and are run here under that profile.
evidence: WP B2-P4-021 story line: acs [], tcs_legacy TC-E2-027-01 to TC-E2-027-13. Legacy section 7 holds AC1 to AC10 only, all on JOB-07 and the PAYMENT_MATCH rows; legacy section 16 marks TC-11 and TC-12 as Access with no AC reference.
proposed: Accept the seven new criteria as the authority evidence of REQ-CHO-009 and review them with the security administrator together with the P8 match criteria; add a legacy access criterion only if the story master is revised.
